source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #281 (branch fix/279-elem-tableidx at head b981705af163e9b9a04d5603aed1b6176f73603d — branch commit a20c782 (parser validates kind-6 element segments against the declared table (#279)) plus merge commit b981705 bringing in current main bfa7df4, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45184156762 and 45184172624 against the branch and pull-request run 45184047623, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #281 (#279, the parser validates kind-6 element segments against table 0 instead of the declared table: parse_elem parsed the segment's tableidx and checked the table exists, but passed a literal 0 to validate_active_elem, so a segment declared for another table was type-checked against table 0's element type — externref segments declared for a funcref table were accepted and funcref segments for such a table were rejected; the fix passes the parsed tableidx, one line in parser/core/parser.rs, plus a new regression suite tests/elem_validation.rs). The branch merged current main (bfa7df4, containing PRs #269, #273, #278, #275, #276 and #280) before measurement; the merge was conflict-free. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (bfa7df4) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45184187750, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. 14 of the 32 gated series change, each by exactly +16 B in both the stripped file and stripped .text sizes, confined to configurations that link the parser (release component / wasi / wasi-threads; release-size core / component / core-jit / wasi-threads); the remaining 18 series are byte-identical. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.37% (1,169,031 B to 1,231,751 B), up from +5.36%. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
